title: Tor vanishing detected by geometric strict henselian local rings
statement:
Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $M$ be any $R$-module and $n\ge0$. For each geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$ [def-weil-geometric-point] with image $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}A$, set $A_{\mathfrak p}=\mathcal O_{X,\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $B_{\bar x}=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{X,\bar x}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Give Tor its coefficient-module action as in [def-trf-tor-coefficient-module]. All $R$-actions are induced by the canonical composite $R\to A\to A_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\bar x}$. Tor and tensor products are those of [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and localization of modules is as in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. The canonical coefficient map is an isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Tor}^{R}_n(M,A)_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak p}}B_{\bar x}\;\xrightarrow{\sim}\;\operatorname{Tor}^{R}_n(M,B_{\bar x}).$$
Moreover,
$$\operatorname{Tor}^{R}_n(M,A)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\operatorname{Tor}^{R}_n(M,B_{\bar x})=0\text{ for every geometric point }\bar x\text{ of }X.$$

source.place: Tag 07QM, lemma-dumb-properties-henselization (faithful flatness); combined with the fixed-base coefficient version of the free-resolution argument of algebra.tex, Tag 00M8, lemma-flat-base-change-tor, and localization in the coefficient ring. Re-split of the original second proof step.

proof.text: Fix $\bar x$ over $\mathfrak p$, and let $K\subset\Omega$ be the separable algebraic closure of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ in the geometric field $\Omega$. Since $\Omega$ is algebraically closed, $K$ is a separable closure of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ by [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure]; $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is the residue field of the local ring $A_{\mathfrak p}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples] to the ring $A_{\mathfrak p}$, its maximal ideal $\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$ and $K$: the category of its etale residue triples is filtered, and its colimit $H$, with structural map $\rho:A_{\mathfrak p}\to H$, is a local ring. By [lem-sc-etale-triples-colimit-is-strict-henselization] (at the closed point, with $\chi:\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to K$ the inclusion), $H$ with this cocone is an algebraic strict henselization of $A_{\mathfrak p}$ relative to $K$. Apply [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison] to the identity open immersion $i:\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$, the point $\bar x$, $L=A_{\mathfrak p}$ and $L^{\mathrm{sh}}=H$. It gives a ring isomorphism $\theta:B_{\bar x}\to H$ with $\theta\circ a=\rho\circ\lambda$, where $a:A\to B_{\bar x}$ is the colimit leg of the chart and $\lambda:A\to A_{\mathfrak p}$ the localization map. Hence $a$ sends $A\setminus\mathfrak p$ to units, and the canonical map $A_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\bar x}$ is the unique ring map through which $a$ factors [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property]. It equals $\theta^{-1}\circ\rho$, since both agree after precomposition with $\lambda$. By [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat] applied to $A_{\mathfrak p}$, $K$ and this cocone, $\rho$ is faithfully flat. Since $\theta$ is an isomorphism of $A_{\mathfrak p}$-algebras, $A_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\bar x}$ is faithfully flat, and the composite from $R$ is the one in the statement.

source.place: Tag 04HX, lemma-describe-etale-local-ring; algebra.tex Tag 04GW, lemma-strict-henselization-different, and Proposition Tag 00CP, proposition-universal-property-localization; more-algebra.tex Tag 07QM, lemma-dumb-properties-henselization (1).

proof.text: Put $T=\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,A)$. By [lem-trf-tor-localization-on-spec], the canonical map $\lambda:T_{\mathfrak p}\to\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,A_{\mathfrak p})$ is an isomorphism. Apply [lem-trf-tor-flat-base-change] to $R\to A_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\bar x}$, using Step 1. Tensor $\lambda$ with $B_{\bar x}$ and compose with that coefficient-base-change isomorphism. This gives the displayed isomorphism. It is the canonical coefficient map: for $t\in T$, $s\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$ and $b\in B_{\bar x}$, it sends $(t/s)\otimes b$ to $b\,s^{-1}\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,A\to B_{\bar x})(t)$. Indeed the two factors are the canonical localization and coefficient maps, so their composite has exactly this formula; these tensors generate the source.

source.place: Tag 00M8, lemma-flat-base-change-tor, fixed-base coefficient-resolution argument; canonical maps as in Tag 00M7, section-functoriality-tor.

proof.text: If $T=0$, then $T_{\mathfrak p}=0$ by the fraction construction [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Its tensor product with $B_{\bar x}$ is zero: every pure tensor has first factor zero [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Step 2 therefore gives $\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,B_{\bar x})=0$ for every geometric point.

source.place: Definitions of module localization and tensor product; forward implication by the isomorphism of Step 2.

proof.text: Conversely assume all geometric coefficient Tor groups vanish. For any prime $\mathfrak p$, choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ by [lem-pc-algebraic-closure-exists-unique]. The point/residue-field description in [def-weil-geometric-point] gives a geometric point over $\mathfrak p$. Apply the faithful-flat descent clause of [lem-trf-tor-flat-base-change] to $R\to A_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\bar x}$, faithfully flat by Step 1. It yields $\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,A_{\mathfrak p})=0$. This holds for every prime, so the final clause of [lem-trf-tor-localization-on-spec] gives $T=0$. If $A$ is the zero ring, there are no primes and $T=0$ already, since its coefficient $A$-module is zero; the cited localization criterion includes this case.

mathlib_searches.query: Tor vanishing can be checked after localization at primes and strict henselization using faithful flatness.
For a ring map R to A with Spec A locally Noetherian, Tor over R of M and A vanishes if and only if it vanishes with every geometric strict henselian local ring of Spec A.
